newsDocuments.headline: Gold eases as oil-driven inflation worries weigh

segments.text: NEW YORK: Gold eased on Tuesday as firmer oil prices fuelled inflation concerns, while investors awaited next week’s Federal Reserve meeting for further direction on US interest rates. Spot gold fell 0.51 percent to USD4,118.76 per ounce by

“Oil is over USD100, so I think basically the story this morning is just a stronger, higher-priced oil is putting pressure on precious metals,” said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX. Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Bre

Gold is still down around 26.4 percent from its record high of USD5,594.82 in January and roughly 22 percent from levels at the start of the Iran war, when concerns over energy inflation reinforced bets on interest rate hikes.

newsDocuments.headline: Govt raises petrol price by Re0.88, diesel by Re0.53 per litre

segments.text: The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Re0.88 to Rs382.02 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.53 to Rs389.80 per litre, effective October 21, 2026.

According to a press release issued by the Petroleum Division, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) revised the ex-depot prices of petroleum products in line with the pricing mechanism set by the federal government.
The Petroleum Division said the change was necessitated by global developments, including movements in Platts rates, premiums and incidentals.
